s: A company needs to migrate some Oracle databases to AWS while keeping otherson-premises for compliance. The on-prem databases contain spatial dataand runcron jobs. The solution must allow querying on-prem data as foreign tables from AWS.
o: Use DynamoDB, SCT, and Lambda. Move spatial data to S3 and query with Athena.
Use RDS for SQL Server and AWS Glue crawlers for Oracle access.
Use EC2-hosted Oracle with Application Migration Service. Use Step Functions for cron.
Use RDS for PostgreSQL with DMS and SCT. Use PostgreSQL foreign data wrappers. Connect via Direct Connect.
e: D is correct because RDS for PostgreSQLsupportsforeign data wrappers (FDW)that allow querying remote Oracle databases. With AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)and Database Migration Service (DMS), schema and data can be migrated effectively.AWS Direct Connect ensures secure, private connectivity to on-prem databases. Cron jobs can be run via EventBridge or external orchestration. A doesn't support relational/spatial querying. B doesn't support FDW or spatial types. C introduces unnecessary complexity. Reference:https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/postgresfdw.html https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.PostgreSQL.html

w.y: The key requirement is querying on-premises Oracle data as foreign tables from AWS. PostgreSQL foreign data wrappers (such as oracle_fdw) provide exactly that, RDS for PostgreSQL with DMS and SCT handles the migrated databases, and Direct Connect gives the private link back to on premises.

o.A: DynamoDB and Athena cannot query on-premises Oracle tables as foreign tables, and moving spatial data to S3 drops the database features.
o.B: Glue crawlers catalog data; they do not provide live foreign-table queries from SQL Server to Oracle.
o.C: Oracle on EC2 lacks the foreign-table requirement as stated and adds self-managed database overhead.
o.D: Correct: RDS for PostgreSQL with foreign data wrappers can query the remaining on-premises Oracle data over Direct Connect.
